document.title: Pakistan - Poll Shows Strong and Growing Public Support for Taleban
document.authors: Carl W. Ford Jr., Assistant Secretary of State for Intelligence and Research, to Secretary Powell
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), Pakistan: "The Taliban's Godfather"?
document.note: [Unclassified] A post-9/11 INR poll shows the Pakistani public more pro-Taliban than before September 11, even as the Musharraf government distances Pakistan from its longstanding Taliban alliance.

events.description: September 11 attacks; polling began shortly afterward.
INR memo to the Secretary reporting poll showing growing Pakistani public support for the Taleban.
Start of bombing in Afghanistan; almost all poll interviews completed before this.
September 11 attacks, after which Pakistani public opinion became more favorable to the Taliban.
INR polling in Pakistan began shortly after September 11, with almost all interviews completed before bombing in Afghanistan.
Ford sends memo to Secretary Powell reporting poll showing strong and growing Pakistani public support for the Taliban.
Start of US bombing in Afghanistan, after which polling was largely complete.
Pakistani government distanced itself from the Taliban after September 11.

key_claims: Pakistani public opinion was more favorable toward the Taleban after September 11 than before.
52% viewed the Taleban more favorably, up nearly 20 points since June 2001.
46% favored strengthening government support for the Taliban, up from 38% in June.
A sizable majority believed the Taleban were not a regional threat and that Pakistan's ties were good.
Musharraf's alignment with the US was difficult and dangerous given public opinion.
